requirement: The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct agents to show the edits a review made to requirements outside its group in the same way as {cite}`requirements.cli.requirements_review_skill.present.mechanical` requires. It MUST also direct them to list every `{example}` a review added and to say that each one needs a test.
rationale:
The subject requires the `habeas-requirements` skill to do three things:
1. Direct agents to show edits made outside a group's own text in the same way as `requirements.cli.requirements_review_skill.present.mechanical`. That means a diff against the agreed or user-supplied text, followed by a list of the mechanical changes.
2. Direct agents to list every `{example}` a review added.
3. Direct agents to say that each added example needs a test.

The test is `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_shows_edits_outside_a_group_and_added_examples]`. It calls `assert_in_order` on the bundled `habeas-requirements` skill. That helper builds the skill text from `SKILL.md` and its reference files, collapses whitespace (`fn[collapse]`), and uses `assert_text_in_order`, which panics if a phrase is missing or comes before the previous one. The two phrases it checks are:
- "as a diff against that text, then a \"Mechanical:\" list". This is the "same way" convention: a diff, then a Mechanical list.
- "Show the edits reviewers made outside their group the same way, and list added `{example}`s, which each need a test". This covers the outside-group edits, the list of added examples, and the statement that each needs a test.

The order assertion requires the outside-group sentence to come after the diff-plus-Mechanical convention. That matches the "same way as" dependency. The skill text in `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md`, workflow step 4, contains both phrases in that order.

The mechanical requirement itself (not raising mechanical changes as questions, and the diff plus Mechanical list for agreed text) is a cited context requirement. `the_requirements_skill_shows_mechanical_changes_without_asking` tests it separately, so it needs no reassessment here.

The assertions are on the exact guidance text, which is the only way to test skill content. A skill that omitted any of the three directions would fail the test. I found no gaps.

text: The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct agents to show the edits a review made to requirements outside its group in the same way as {cite}`requirements.cli.requirements_review_skill.present.mechanical` requires. It MUST also direct them to list every `{example}` a review added and to say that each one needs a test.

The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct agents not to raise mechanical changes to new text as questions. For text that was already agreed or that the user supplied, it MUST direct agents to show the change as a diff against that text, followed by a list of the mechanical changes.
